newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypy's parliament lifts MP's immunity.
newsitem.headline: Egypy's parliament lifts MP's immunity.

text.p: Egypt's parliament has lifted the immunity of an Islamist MP to allow an investigation into allegations that he is a member of the outlawed but influential Moslem Brotherhood, house sources said on Monday.
Local media have said the public prosecutor wanted to question Labour Party member Ali Sayyed Fath al-Bab on suspicion that he was involved with a group of 53 alleged Brotherhood members.
"A memo by the state security... said that Fath al-Bab, member of parliament for the southern Cairo constituency of Tibeen is one of the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood's leaders," a source said.
The spokesman for the Brotherhood did not comment on claims Fath al-Bab was a member.
"The whole issue is a farce. It is clear that they (the government) do not want to have any Islamist in the parliament," Brotherhood spokesman Mamoun Hudaibi told Reuters.
Fath al-Bab is the only parliamentarian who belongs to the opposition Labour Party, which has Islamist tendencies.
Hudaibi said that parliament generally lifted an MP's immunity after there was enough evidence unearthed to convict, but in this case they had voted on mere suspicion.
"It is a warning to all members," he said, adding that any police officer now can prepare a report against any parliamentarian to get his immunity lifted.
The Labour Party contains many members of the Brotherhood, which repeatedly has been denied legal recognition as a political party.

For many years the state tolerated the Brotherhood, a large and influential organisation, but for the past two years it has tried to equate it with the violent groups trying to overthrow the government by force.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since 1992 when Moslem militant groups began their armed struggle for power but Brotherhood leaders say they oppose the use of violence for political ends.
